metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Inactive with shoulder injury
metadata.description: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus battled a shoulder injury throughout Week 7 prep, logging limited practice participation in all three sessions. The wide receiver ultimately lost the battle and will need additional time to recover from the injury, leaving Zachariah Branch as the Falcons' No. 3 wide receiver for Sunday's contest against the 49ers.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Trending down for Week 7
metadata.description: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is trending toward not being available for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus was limited by a shoulder issue in all three practices of Week 7 prep. That earned him the questionable tag for Sunday's game, but it looks like the veteran wide receiver will miss his first game of the 2026 season. Zachariah Branch would take on a larger role offensively and on special teams as a returner if Zaccheaus is unable to play.

metadata.title: Falcons Not Optimistic That Olamide Zaccheaus Will Play in Week 7
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), who is listed as questionable, appears to be trending in the wrong direction for Week 7 against the San Francisco 49ers, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. When comparing Zaccheaus' status to his teammates, Rapoport said that the Falcons have "much less optimism" for the veteran receiver. The 29-year-old has merely been a depth option this season. Even though he logged a season-high 55% snap share and four targets last week, he was held without a reception. He has just four receptions this season, and he hasn't caught a single pass since Week 3. Zaccheaus can be left on waivers in all fantasy leagues. Drake London remains the only must-roster and must-start Falcons wide receiver, but Jahan Dotson has also started to generate some buzz after catching seven passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns over his last three games.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Questionable for Week 7
metadata.description: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus practice reps were limited during Week 7 prep due to a shoulder issue, which he may have picked up during the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. If he cannot play Sunday, then rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch would be in line for more work both on offense and on special teams as a returner, with running back Brian Robinson also in the mix for return duties.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Logs another limited practice
metadata.description: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: It's the second straight limited practice to begin the week for Zaccheaus, who is dealing with a shoulder injury. He may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid being tagged with a designation heading into the weekend. Zaccheaus had four catches on six targets through three weeks but hasn't caught any of his five targets over Atlanta's past three contests.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) limited participant Wednesday
metadata.description: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to log a full practice on Wednesday, as he was left limited by a shoulder injury of some kind. Rookie Zachariah Branch may see more work if the veteran has to miss any time.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Limited practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus appears to have picked up a shoulder injury during the team's 31-23 loss to the Bears in Week 6. The fact that he was able to practice in any capacity Wednesday would suggest that it is a minor issue, but the wide receiver will have two more chances to prove his health before Sunday's matchup with the 49ers.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus sees four targets in Week 6
metadata.description: Olamide Zaccheaus failed to catch any of his four targets in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 6.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus has struggled to make an impact to this point, posting two receptions or less in each of the first six contests. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 7 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Just one target Monday
metadata.description: Zaccheaus failed to haul in his lone target during the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday.
metadata.analysis: The Falcons relied more heavily on the running game Monday, with Michael Penix attempting only 20 passes while Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 203 yards and five touchdowns on 33 carries. That left few targets to go around for the Falcons' pass catchers, with none other than Drake London (six) seeing more than three targets from quarterback Michael Penix. Zaccheaus' 21 offensive snaps were third-most among Falcons wide receivers behind London (51) and Jahan Dotson (36). However, despite entering the season as the team's WR3, Zaccheaus has just four catches (on seven targets) for 17 yards through the first four games of the regular season, and rookie wideout Zachariah Branch has seemingly taken over as Atlanta's primary returner on kickoffs and special teams. Up next for the Falcons is a Week 5 home showdown against the Ravens.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Two catches in Thursday's win
metadata.description: Zaccheaus brought in both of his targets for nine yards and returned one punt for four yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Both of Zaccheaus' catches occurred in the second quarter on the same drive, which ended with a 44-yard field goal by Nick Folk. Zaccheaus is up to four catches (on six targets) for 17 yards through three regular-season games while operating as a depth option in the passing game, though Thursday's win may have been the start for a more explosive offense for the Falcons with Michael Penix under center, rather than Tua Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (coach's decision) or Jack Strand (coach's decision). The Falcons will travel to New Orleans to face the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Plays versatile role in loss
metadata.description: Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for three yards while returning four kicks for 79 yards in Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus played 30 offensive snaps and seven special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver and returner is a jack-of-all-trades, filling in and assisting wherever he can for a Falcons team that lacks depth in multiple areas due to injuries.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Catches sole target amidst many roles
metadata.description: Zaccheaus caught his sole target for five yards and returned one kick for 29 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus was the Falcons' WR3, QB3, and RB3 in Sunday's contest while also being the No. 2 kick and punt returner. The Renaissance man played many roles for the team but did not have a big night by the box score or snap logs. Zaccheaus played just 18 of the 60 offensive snaps for the Falcons and just five special teams snaps.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Jack-of-all-trades for Week 1
metadata.description: Zaccheaus will serve as the Falcons' WR3, the backup returner on punts and kickoffs, and the emergency third option at both quarterback and running back for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Steelers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The Falcons have two quarterbacks (Cooper Rush and Jack Strand) and two running backs (Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson) on the game-day roster for Sunday's regular-season opener. Most of Zaccheaus' playing time figures to come on three-wideout sets as he works behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson, with rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch also in the mix for offensive snaps.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus to Serve as Emergency Third QB, RB
metadata.description: With both quarterbacks Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) ruled out for the Week 1 season opener on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus will be the team's emergency third QB behind Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. And with the Falcons having only two running backs active -- Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson -- Zaccheaus will also be the team's emergency third-string running back. While this does not move the needle at all in fantasy for Zaccheaus, it speaks to his versatility and athleticism on the football field. The 29-year-old former undrafted free agent from Virginia has never had more than 45 receptions, 533 yards, or three touchdowns in a single season in his seven years in the NFL with the Falcons, Eagles, Commanders, and Bears. Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two scores in 16 regular-season games in 2025 with the Bears, and he opens up the 2026 season as the Falcons' WR3 behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus has Interesting Upside as Starter
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus has been quietly moving up draft boards recently. In the latest unofficial depth chart, Zaccheaus is listed as a starter ahead of rookie Zachariah Branch. The expectation is that Zaccheaus will remain a starter to begin the season while Branch gets more comfortable as a pro. Down the road, Zaccheaus could lose playing time, but he might be a deep league option to begin the season. The Falcons are going to lean on Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. as their focal points in the passing game. They also have stud running back leading the charge on the ground. There might not be a ton of work for Zaccheaus, but he could be worth stashing in deep leagues to begin the year.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus Holding Onto a Starting Role
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus has quietly improved his redraft outlook by holding onto a starting role as the preseason winds down. Atlanta's latest unofficial depth chart still lists Zaccheaus with the first team, ahead of rookie Zachariah Branch in the slot. The game usage has backed that up. In the preseason opener, Zaccheaus played six of eight first-team snaps with Tua Tagovailoa, while Branch saw just one. The Falcons then sat Zaccheaus, Drake London, and Jahan Dotson against Indianapolis, and Branch remained mostly with the reserves. Zaccheaus also moved outside during a two-minute drill in joint practices so Atlanta could get Branch onto the field in the slot, showing there is at least a path for both to play. The 29-year-old caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns with Chicago last season after posting 45 catches for 506 yards and three scores with Washington in 2024. London, Dotson, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson will limit the ceiling, and Branch remains a threat to earn more work. Still, Zaccheaus has done enough to enter Week 1 as the favorite for a meaningful complementary role.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Open competition for WR2
metadata.description: Zaccheaus enters training camp in a battle against Jahan Dotson and rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch for the Falcons' WR2 job behind Drake London (undisclosed), Tim Weaver of USA Today reports.
metadata.analysis: After stints in Philadelphia, Washington and Chicago, Zaccheaus opted to sign a one-year contract in March to rejoin the Falcons, whom he played four seasons for from 2019 to 2022. The Virginia product has eclipsed 500 receiving yards just once in the first seven years of his NFL career, but given the lack of reliable pass catchers behind London and tight end Kyle Pitts, Zaccheaus will have the chance to establish himself as Atlanta's WR2 in training camp. Dotson brings four years of NFL experience to the table, but Zaccheaus' biggest competition figures to come from the rookie Branch, who made a strong impression on coaches and players for his speed, explosiveness and playmaking ability during college and in OTAs.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus Battling for WR2 Job in Atlanta This Summer
metadata.description: Tim Weaver of Falcons Wire writes that Atlanta Falcons wide receivers Olamide Zaccheaus, Jahan Dotson, and rookie Zachariah Branch will battle for the WR2 job in training camp this summer behind Drake London. Dotson, a former first-rounder by the Philadelphia Eagles, is the most logical option, but he hasn't been anything special in the NFL since he caught 35 passes for 523 yards and seven touchdowns in 12 games as a rookie in 2022. Weaver points out that Zaccheaus has the upper hand in terms of experience, having played in 105 games (35 starts), catching 188 passes for 2,311 yards and 15 touchdowns in seven years with four different teams. Branch, meanwhile, has the most pure upside thanks to his speed and playmaking ability in space. Weaver writes that it's "truly a wide-open competition." Zaccheaus is returning to Atlanta after starting his career with the Falcons in 2019 and playing with them through the 2022 campaign. He has only topped 500 receiving yards once in his seven seasons, but given the lack of depth and experience behind London and tight end Kyle Pitts Sr., Zaccheaus could be worth a late-round dart throw in deep leagues for the opportunity.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus - Returning to Atlanta
metadata.description: Zaccheaus is in line to sign with the Falcons, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus previously played for Atlanta from 2019 to 2022, under Dan Quinn and Arthur Smith. The team now is led by Kevin Stefanski, who is badly in need of depth to support RB Bijan Robinson, WR Drake London and TE Kyle Pitts at the skill positions. Zaccheaus fits best as a No. 3/4 receiver, but he might get a crack at the No. 2 role if the Falcons don't bring in a bigger name. They're expected to release WR Darnell Mooney on Wednesday when the 2026 league year begins.

metadata.title: Olamide Zaccheaus signs with Atlanta Falcons
metadata.description: Olamide Zaccheaus has signed with the Atlanta Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Zaccheaus began his NFL career in Atlanta, and now finds his way back home. He'll likely factor in as a special teams man and depth behind Drake London. Don't expect the Falcons to end their WR moves here.
